reason: The rover needs to cross loose sand, so metal stock and cargo mesh might make a traction aid.
expectation: I expect to make some kind of traction mat or support for the crossing, though I’m not sure how it will be used.

alternatives.reason: Sieving gravel might also help prepare the crossing, but a mesh mat seems more directly useful under the wheels.

effect: The panels are a traction aid, and their raised edges suggest gravel will help them support the wheels.
reaction: The way the mesh holds gravel makes the crossing plan clearer.
reason: Sieving the firm gravel patch is the only available combination and seems likely to prepare material for the panels.
expectation: I expect to collect or grade gravel for the traction panels, though I’m unsure exactly how the sieve will be used.

effect: The sieve produced coarse gravel, which appears ready to fill the traction panels.
reaction: The result fits the crossing plan, though it adds little explanation.
reason: Combining the gravel and panels is the only offered gameplay action and should prepare the traction aid.
expectation: I expect gravel-filled panels that can support the rover’s wheels over the loose sand.

effect: The filled tracks complete the crossing preparation and clarify how the frames keep the supporting gravel in place.
reaction: The explanation makes the assembled tracks satisfying, though I’m curious about the ice exposure beyond the crossing.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the traction panels was most worthwhile: their mesh bottoms and raised edges gave me a practical picture of how they could support wheels in loose ground.

leastWorthwhile.text: Sieving the gravel was the least engaging step; the result named the material but offered little explanation.

surprise.text: The panels hold gravel as well as spreading the wheel’s weight; I had expected a traction mat but not that particular construction.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary. Once the panels were made, the remaining combinations followed clearly from their need for gravel, though each was the only available gameplay action.

continue.text: Yes. I want to see what happens at the ice exposure and whether the intact core reveals more about the specimen, though this chapter ended before the crossing itself.
